subject: GMR-Gal4 dotprops registered to JFRC2 or JRC2018 unisex template

messages.author: a7b4b8806b78ccd8
messages.subject: GMR-Gal4 dotprops registered to JFRC2 or JRC2018 unisex template
parts:
Hi all,

I have started using the desktop version of nblast using nat.nblast and I am trying to compute similarity scores of my traced neurons against GMR-Gal4 lines. My traced neurons are registered to the JFRC2 or JRC 2018 Unisex space. I wonder if there exists GMR-Gal4 dotprops for these templates. If possible, I prefer not to go through the additional step of bridging between JFRC2/JRC2018 to FCWB.

Thanks
Ibrahim

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: GMR-Gal4 dotprops registered to JFRC2 or JRC2018 unisex template
parts:
Dear Ibrahim,

I am afraid I am not quite sure where we are with dotprops libraries for those other templates. We surely had them for JFRC2 at some point. However I would also say there is no reason not to convert your neurons to FCWB and search with those.

All the best,

Greg.

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Re: GMR-Gal4 dotprops registered to JFRC2 or JRC2018 unisex template
parts: On 13 Nov 2020, at 08:29, Ibrahim Taştekin <ibrahim....@research.fchampalimaud.org> wrote:

Thanks so much for your reply! I am still not able to use CMTK on my Windows machine (could not solve the Error in cmtk.streamxform(points, reg, direction, transformtype)). That is why, I just tried my chances :)

Ah sorry. It's a shame that windows is difficult. There are recommendations about how to install CMTK for windows from users here:

https://www.nitrc.org/forum/forum.php?thread_id=11060&forum_id=857
However, I just finished creating a JFRC2>FCWB bridge in ANTs and now I can do a batch registration of my neurons!

Ah. There should already a registration path to FCWB using the nat.jrcbrains package. This uses a java tool from Stephan Saalfeld and colleagues at Janelia not CMTK.

However, I would recommend using the original CMTK transform for this purpose. The reasoning is as follows:

The CMTK bridging registration from JFRC2->FCWB is not the highest quality because different antibody stains are used for the two template brains.

The FCWB dotprops objects for the GMR-GAL4 data were transformed using this CMTK registration. If you transform your tracings using this bridging registration then any errors in the transform will not matter. If you use a different bridging registration (which will also be low quality for the same reasons) then you will have different errors.

All the best,

Greg.

Bridging registrations after doing:
library(nat.flybrains)
 

library(nat.jrcbrains)
